requirement:
An mdBook chapter MAY declare a named definition using a fenced `{definition}` directive. Definitions MUST use the same chapter-qualified names, identifier rules, fence rules, and nonempty-body rules as requirements and examples. Names MUST be unique across all three kinds.

Each definition MUST declare exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` option before its explanatory body. The phrase MUST be interpreted as plain text. Definitions MUST NOT require their own evidence records or determinations.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every MUST/MUST NOT obligation has marked implementing code and a test that asserts its outcome.

**Shared names, identifier rules, fence rules and nonempty-body rules.**
- `definition_blocks` (src/lib.rs) recognizes `{definition}` with the same fence, colon-count and name parsing as `{req}` and `{example}`.
- `collect_definitions` (src/evidence.rs) applies `valid_name`, the closing-fence check and the "has no text" check to all three kinds.
- `tests/definitions.rs::definitions_share_name_and_fence_rules_and_need_no_evidence` checks an invalid chapter namespace ("bad dir.terms.a") and a four-colon fence that holds a shorter colon line in its body.
- `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` checks the "missing a closing colon fence" error for an unclosed definition.

**Names unique across all three kinds.**
- `collect_definitions` uses one `definitions` map for all kinds, so a clash produces "duplicate definition …".
- The same test declares `{req} x` and `{definition} x` in one chapter and asserts "duplicate definition bad.x".

**Exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` option before the body.**
- `terms::declaration` (src/terms.rs) rejects a missing phrase, an empty phrase, an empty body, and a second `:phrase:` line directly after the first.
- `collect_definitions` calls it and reports "definition {name}: …".
- The test `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` loops over four bad bodies: body only, empty phrase, duplicate phrase, and phrase only. It asserts the "definition bad.bad:" error for each.

**Phrase interpreted as plain text.**
- `terms::escaped_phrase` escapes Markdown and HTML characters.
- `replace_definitions` uses it when rendering a definition.
- `phrases_are_plain_links_and_markdown_literals_are_preserved` asserts that `*alpha* & <beta>` renders as `*alpha* & <beta>`.

**No evidence records or determinations.**
- `inspect_repository_with_progress` filters out `DefinitionKind::Term` when matching evidence files, so a definition never counts as expected evidence.
- The missing-evidence loop skips `DefinitionKind::Term`.
- `validate_references` excludes terms from its `subjects` list.
- The test `definitions_share_name_and_fence_rules_and_need_no_evidence` asserts that no "glossary." errors appear, while the requirement `rules.ready` does report "evidence/rules.ready.json: missing".

I saw no marking gaps. The helpers `noun` and `badge`, and `reference_roles`, carry {impl} references. I found no unspecified behavior that the text or the other requirements these items mark don't cover.
